record.title: Complex KDA extends Kimi Delta Attention state-transition expressivity
record.summary: Complex KDA (CKDA) combines two parameter-range extensions—signed channel gates and a delta coefficient up to 2—to make Kimi Delta Attention express 2D rotations using a single diagonal-plus-rank-one recurrent transition. The paper proves exact representability for orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one matrices and reports finite-group state-tracking, synthetic periodic-audio and language-model experiments. The authors report stronger length extrapolation on selected synthetic tasks and language-model results comparable to KDA, not a broad demonstrated language-model advantage. Open code and committed measurements aid inspection; no independent proof audit or training reproduction was conducted.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper extends Kimi Delta Attention’s gate range to [-1,1] and delta coefficient to [0,2], allowing a single delta-rule update plus a channel-wise gate reflection to represent 2D rotations while retaining a diagonal-plus-rank-one transition.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors prove that every orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one matrix is exactly representable as a Complex KDA transition, and report finite-group state-tracking and periodic-waveform experiments with stronger length extrapolation than the tested KDA range settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In language-model experiments, the authors report results comparable to a KDA baseline and promising scaling behavior; the public repository includes committed experiment tables and reproduction code, but this review did not rerun the training.

contradictory_evidence: The authors explicitly report that CKDA language-model results are similar to the KDA baseline, which limits any claim of current language-model performance gains.
The audio task is intentionally restricted to extrapolating circular shifts of one synthetic groove; the repository notes that a GRU remains strongest on that task.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent review of the exact representability proof or reproduction of the reported finite-group, audio or language-model results was performed.
Practical effects on quality, long-context behavior and compute at larger language-model scales are not established by the bounded paper experiments.

brief.importance_rationale: If the expressivity theorem and reported behavior hold, a single low-rank recurrent transition can represent transformations that otherwise require composing transitions, which could alter architecture and state-tracking choices while retaining linear-update structure. Current consequence is meaningful but bounded: language-model results are reported as comparable to KDA, and broad practical benefit is not established.
limitations: All empirical results are author-reported; this review did not independently reproduce them or audit the proof.
The finite-group tasks use one recurrent layer and bounded sequence-length extrapolation; periodic audio is a synthetic fixed-groove task rather than general audio generation.
The paper reports language-model results comparable to its KDA baseline and only describes scaling behavior as promising; it does not establish a broad downstream advantage.
The public repository archives measurements and provides reproduction drivers, but rerunning large language-model training requires external compute.
brief.summary: Complex KDA (CKDA) combines two parameter-range extensions—signed channel gates and a delta coefficient up to 2—to make Kimi Delta Attention express 2D rotations using a single diagonal-plus-rank-one recurrent transition. The paper proves exact representability for orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one matrices and reports finite-group state-tracking, synthetic periodic-audio and language-model experiments. The authors report stronger length extrapolation on selected synthetic tasks and language-model results comparable to KDA, not a broad demonstrated language-model advantage. Open code and committed measurements aid inspection; no independent proof audit or training reproduction was conducted.

technical.claimed_result: The authors prove exact representability within the stated matrix class and report improved length extrapolation among tested KDA range settings on selected synthetic tasks, while language-model results are comparable to KDA.
technical.compute_or_cost: No independent compute or cost accounting was performed. The repository states that full training reproduction requires an external training stack and accelerator resources.
technical.demonstrated_result: No independent demonstration by this review. The paper and repository report the theorem, empirical results, configs and archived measurement tables.
technical.implementation_status: Open implementation and experiment drivers are available in the OpenEuroLLM repository. The repository contains committed measurements; this review inspected the README/index but did not run the artifacts or train models.
technical.mechanism: Extend KDA channel gate α to [-1,1] and delta-rule coefficient β to [0,2]. A single delta-rule transition plus a gate reflection then represents 2D rotations while preserving diagonal-plus-rank-one, non-expansive transitions.
technical.novelty: The paper claims exact representation of every orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one transition matrix in this parameterization, without composing two delta transitions.
technical.regime: Theory for the stated transition family; author experiments include single-layer finite-group state tracking on S3/S4/A5, synthetic periodic-waveform extrapolation and language-model training/scaling experiments.
technical.reproducibility: Public code, configs and committed experiment tables support inspection and partial reproduction. Large model training is not executed here; exact numerical results remain author-reported.
technical.strongest_baseline: KDA range settings and DeltaProduct2-style composed transitions in the paper’s matched expressivity/state-tracking comparisons; KDA is the direct language-model baseline.

brief.title: Complex KDA extends Kimi Delta Attention state-transition expressivity
brief.why_it_matters: The result identifies a way to expand the state transformations available to a linear recurrent layer without increasing its transition rank, which could change memory and recurrence design choices. The strongest support is a mathematical paper claim with open experiment artifacts; practical gains beyond the tested tasks and language-model setup remain unverified.
